extraction_notes: Non-alloy pig iron, P <= 0.5% by weight (description '05 percent or less' = 0.5%, upper bound). predominant=iron.
Non-alloy pig iron, P > 0.5% by weight (lower bound). High-phosphorus pig iron.
Alloy pig iron — cast iron (7201.50 = alloy pig iron and spiegeleisen).
Other alloy pig iron / spiegeleisen (residual under 7201.50).
High-carbon ferro-manganese, C > 2% (lower bound). Ferro-alloy per Ch.72 Note 1(c). predominant=manganese (named alloy element).
Other (medium/low carbon) ferro-manganese, C <= 2%. carbon_pct upper bound = 2.0.
High-silicon ferro-silicon, Si > 55% (lower bound). Used as deoxidizer in steelmaking.
Ferro-silico-manganese — dual alloy. Predominant alloy element = manganese (Mn typically 60-70% vs Si 15-25%).
High-carbon ferro-chromium (HC FeCr), C > 4% (lower bound). predominant=chromium.
Ferro-silico-chromium dual alloy. Predominant = chromium (typically Cr 30-40% vs Si 8-14%).
Ferro-nickel for stainless steel production. predominant=nickel (named alloy element).
Ferro-tungsten AND ferro-silico-tungsten covered jointly. predominant=tungsten.
Ferro-selenium (Indian split under 7202.99). Note: selenium has no dedicated numeric pct field in schema.
Ferro-columbium = legacy US name for ferro-niobium. India retained columbium nomenclature.
Ferro-tantalum (Indian split). Tantalum has no dedicated numeric pct field.
Ferro-silico-magnesium used as nodularizer for SG (ductile) cast iron. Magnesium is the active element though Si is usually higher mass-fraction; predominant=magnesium per functional role.

Charge-chrome = lower-grade Cr ferro-alloy (typically 52-55% Cr, used for stainless steel direct charge). chromium_pct midpoint of typical 52-55% range = 52 (lower bound). predominant=chromium. [F4-fix: chromium_pct cleared — no explicit %-bound in description].
Other unspecified ferro-alloys (residual). predominant=null (alloy not named).
Direct-reduced iron (sponge iron / DRI). India is a major DRI producer.
Cast iron scrap. Heading 7204 = ferrous waste/scrap.
Empty/discharged stainless steel cartridges (subheading 7204.21 = stainless steel scrap).
Empty/discharged alloy steel cartridges (7204.29 = other alloy steel scrap).
High-speed steel (HSS) scrap — Indian-specific 8-digit split for premium tool steel recovery.
Machining-derived scrap: turnings, shavings, chips, sawdust, filings, trimmings, stampings.
Remelting scrap ingots (consolidated scrap recast into ingot form for remelt).
Iron shot/angular grit (granules per 7205.10). Used for surface preparation.
Other granules of iron or steel (residual under 7205.10).
Alloy steel powder per Ch.72 Note 8(b) (passing 1mm sieve >=90% by weight). sieve fields stay null — no explicit grading in description.
Iron ingot (non-alloy-steel ingot per heading 7206). Indian split: 'of iron'.

Note: ITC label here says 'Powders' but the description lists puddled bars/pilings (legacy wrought iron primary forms). Indian Tariff hierarchical label appears mislabeled — content is per description.
Blocks, lumps and similar primary forms under 7206.90.
7207.11 = semi-finished non-alloy steel, rectangular cross-section, width <2x thickness, carbon <0.25% (upper bound). 'Electrical quality' = downstream destined for transformer/motor lamination.
Seamless steel tube quality semi-finished feedstock, C <0.25%.
7207.12 = other rectangular (non-square) cross-section, width >=2x thickness, C <0.25%. Electrical quality.
7207.19 = other (non-rectangular cross-section), C <0.25%. Forged blanks of non-alloy steel.
Mild steel billets (rebar/structural feedstock). Indian-specific 8-digit split.
7207.20 = semi-finished non-alloy steel, C >=0.25% (lower bound 0.25). Forging quality.
7208 = flat-rolled non-alloy steel, width >=600mm, hot-rolled. .10 = in coils, with patterns in relief (chequered plate).
7208.25 = in coils, pickled, thickness >=4.75mm. Indian 8-digit split: Plates.
Universal plates (mill-rolled to width without edging) in 7208.25.
7208.26 = in coils, pickled, thickness 3-<4.75mm. Plate split.
7208.36 = in coils, not pickled, thickness >10mm. Plates.
7208.37 = in coils, not pickled, thickness 4.75-10mm. Plates.
7208.38 = in coils, not pickled, thickness 3-<4.75mm. Plates.
7208.39 = in coils, not pickled, thickness <3mm. Plates.
7208.40 = not in coils, with patterns in relief (chequered plate). Plates split.
7208.51 = not in coils, thickness >10mm. Plates split.
7209.15 = cold-rolled non-alloy steel, in coils, thickness >=3mm (lower bound from subheading definition). Indian 8-digit split .10=Plates (heavier-gauge commercial form).
7209.15 thickness >=3mm in coils; .20=Sheets (Indian split, lighter sheets within heavy-gauge band).
7209.15 cold-rolled in coils >=3mm; .30=Strip Indian split (narrower slit width).
7209.16 = cold-rolled in coils, thickness >1mm to <3mm (HS subheading definition). .10=Plates.
Residual under 7209.16 (1-<3mm cold-rolled coils not plate/sheet/strip).
7209.17 = cold-rolled coils, thickness 0.5-1mm (HS subheading definition). .10=Plates (unusual for this thin gauge but Indian split retained).
7209.17 cold-rolled coils 0.5-1mm; .20=Sheets. Common gauge for auto body panels and appliance shells.
7209.18 = cold-rolled coils, thickness <0.5mm (thinnest CR coil band). .10=Plates Indian split (rare at this gauge).

Description text shows transition: 'Other Not in coils, not further worked than cold-rolled (cold-reduced):' — this .90 line is the bridge to 7209.25-.28 (not in coils). Marked processing_state=not-in-coils per the bridge text.
7209.25 = cold-rolled non-alloy steel, NOT in coils, thickness >=3mm; .10=Plates.
7209.27 = cold-rolled, not in coils, thickness 0.5-1mm; .10=Plates Indian split.
7209.27 cold-rolled not in coils 0.5-1mm; .20=Sheets. Typical CR sheet gauge.
7209.28 cold-rolled not in coils <0.5mm; .20=Sheets. Black plate.
7209.90 = other (further-worked beyond cold-rolling but uncoated, not in subheadings .15-.28).

7210.11 = electrolytically tin-coated, thickness >=0.5mm; .10 OTS/MR = 'Old Tin Sheet / Metal Recovery' Indian commercial grade (lower-quality reclaim tinplate). intended_role=packaging (can-making feedstock).
7210.20 = lead-coated or terne-plated (terne = Pb-Sn alloy coat ~80/20). Used historically for fuel tanks/roofing.
7210.30.91 = galvannealed (zinc-coated then heat-treated to form Fe-Zn alloy surface for improved paint adhesion; common auto-body grade).
7210.41 = otherwise zinc-coated (hot-dip galvanized, NOT electrolytic), corrugated. Classic GI sheet for roofing.
7210.49.10 = hot-dip galvanized then galvannealed (Fe-Zn alloy surface from in-line heat treatment).
7210.50 = ECCS = Electrolytically Chromium Coated Steel (TFS / Tin-Free Steel). Can-making substitute for tinplate.
7210.61 = aluminum-zinc alloy coated (commercially Galvalume / Zincalume, typ. 55%Al-43.4%Zn-1.6%Si). Premium long-life roofing.
7210.69 = other Al-coated (pure Al coating, e.g. Type 1 / Type 2 aluminized for auto exhaust and high-temp applications).
7210.70 = painted/varnished/plastic-coated (PPGI / PPGL pre-painted galvanized/galvalume for color-coated roofing and appliance panels).

7211.13 = 'universal mill plate' description per subheading text — rolled on four faces or in closed box pass, width >150mm, thickness >=4mm, not in coils, no relief patterns. Width <600mm (per heading 7211).
7211.14 = hot-rolled, narrow strip, thickness >=4.75mm, width <600mm. .10=Flats (Indian commercial grade, narrow rectangular cross-section).
7211.14 hot-rolled >=4.75mm <600mm wide; .20=Universal plates (Indian commercial term for mill-edge plate).
7211.14 .30=Hoops (Indian commercial term for narrow hot-rolled strip used as binding hoop / strap).
7211.14 .60=Skelp (narrow HR strip rolled specifically for welded-tube production — Indian commercial term).
7211.19 = hot-rolled, narrow strip, thickness <4.75mm, width <600mm (thinner gauges vs 7211.14). .10=Flats.
7211.23 = cold-rolled non-alloy strip, width <600mm, containing by weight LESS than 0.25% carbon. carbon_pct=0.25 (UPPER bound). .10=Flats.
7211.29 = cold-rolled non-alloy strip <600mm wide, OTHER (i.e. C>=0.25%). carbon_pct=0.25 LOWER bound. .10=Flats.
7211.90 = Other narrow strip (further-worked beyond HR/CR). .11=Universal plates of boiler quality (Indian-specific spec for pressure-vessel manufacture, IS:2002).
7211.90.12 = Universal plates of high-tensile quality (IS:2062 / similar high-strength structural steel).
7211.90.13 = Universal plates of shipbuilding quality (IS:2002 Grade A/B/D/E or LR-approved marine grade).
7211.90.90 = Universal plates, other (residual under 7211.90 — non boiler/HT/ship quality).
7212.10 = tin-coated narrow strip <600mm wide. .10 OTS/MR = Old Tin Sheet/Metal Recovery grade.
7212.30 = otherwise zinc-coated narrow strip (hot-dip galvanized). .10=Corrugated GI narrow strip.
7212.30.91 = hot-dip galvanized then galvannealed narrow strip.
7212.60 = clad narrow strip (mechanically/roll-bonded composite, not coating). Common for stainless-clad or nickel-clad applications.

7213.10 = hot-rolled bars/rods in irregularly-wound coils, with indentations/ribs/grooves (concrete reinforcement / rebar in coils). .10 = free-cutting steel (high-S/Pb for improved machinability — IS:6249/SAE 12L14 family).
7213.10.90 = other ribbed bars/rods in coils (standard rebar in coils per IS:1786 — TMT bar in coil form).
7213.20 = Other free-cutting steel hot-rolled in coils. .10=Electrode quality (Indian commercial spec for stick-welding rod core wire feedstock).
7213.20.20 = Cold-heading quality (CHQ) wire rod for bolt/screw/rivet manufacture (IS:4431).
7213.20.90 = other free-cutting steel hot-rolled in coils.
7213.91 = Other in coils, circular cross-section, diameter <14mm (wire rod). .10=Electrode quality.
7213.91.90 = other circular wire rod <14mm. General wire drawing feedstock.
7213.99 = Other in coils (not circular <14mm). .10=Electrode quality, larger or non-circular section.
7214.10 = forged bars/rods of iron/non-alloy steel. .10=Spring steel quality (Indian commercial grade for leaf/coil springs — typically 55Si7 / 65Si7 type).
7214.20 = bars/rods with indentations/ribs/grooves (rebar) OR twisted after rolling. .10=Spring steel quality (unusual but Indian split retained).
7214.20.90 = other ribbed rebar (TMT bars per IS:1786, Fe415/500/550/600 grades — the workhorse construction rebar).
7214.30 = other free-cutting steel bars/rods, not further worked beyond hot-rolling.
7214.91 = Other, of rectangular (other than square) cross-section. .10 = Mild steel bright bar (cold-finished mild steel, common Indian commercial spec).
7214.99 = Other (round, square, hexagonal, octagonal etc.). .10=Spring steel quality.
7215.10 = other bars/rods of free-cutting steel, cold-formed/cold-finished (bright bar).
7215.50 = Other bars/rods, cold-formed/cold-finished (not free-cutting). .10 = Mild steel bright bar — classic Indian commercial term for cold-drawn mild steel round/square/hex.
7215.90 = Other bars/rods of iron/non-alloy steel (further-worked beyond cold-forming, incl. coatings). .10=Zinc-coated.
7216.10 = U, I or H sections, hot-rolled/drawn/extruded, height <80mm. Light structural sections. intended_role=support (load-bearing structural).
7216.21 = L sections (angles), hot-rolled etc., height <80mm. Light angles per IS:2062.
7216.22 = T sections, hot-rolled etc., height <80mm. Light T-sections.
